migrate_traffic.description: If set to true traffic will be migrated to this version.
migrate_traffic.rationale: Controls whether traffic is gradually migrated to the target version during a split-traffic update. This is a deployment-behaviour/availability choice, not a security control.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: To automatically inherit the provider-level project ID.

service.description: The name of the service these settings apply to.
service.rationale: References the service the traffic-split configuration applies to. This is a reference/identifier to another resource, not a security control.

split.description: Mapping that defines fractional HTTP traffic diversion to different versions within the service.

split.allocations.description: Mapping from version IDs within the service to fractional (0.000, 1] allocations of traffic for that version. Each version can be specified only once, but some versions in the service may not have any traffic allocation. Services that have traffic allocated cannot be deleted until either the service is deleted or their traffic allocation is removed. Allocations must sum to 1. Up to two decimal place precision is supported for IP-based splits and up to three decimal places is supported for cookie-based splits.
split.allocations.rationale: Maps version IDs to fractional shares of incoming traffic for canary/blue-green rollouts. This is a team deployment/routing choice with no generic secure value to enforce, so it is not a platform policy target.

split.shard_by.description: Mechanism used to determine which version a request is sent to. The traffic selection algorithm will be stable for either type until allocations are changed. Possible values: ["UNSPECIFIED", "COOKIE", "IP", "RANDOM"]
split.shard_by.rationale: Selects the mechanism (cookie/IP/random) used to assign a request to a version during traffic splitting. This is a routing/affinity choice, not a security control.
